Static evidence:
- `MutableDateTime.addYears/addMonths/addWeeks/addDays/add(DurationFieldType, int)` all delegate directly to chronology duration fields:
  - [MutableDateTime](/abs/path/org/joda/time/MutableDateTime.java:635)
  - [MutableDateTime](/abs/path/org/joda/time/MutableDateTime.java:659)
  - [MutableDateTime](/abs/path/org/joda/time/MutableDateTime.java:701)
  - [MutableDateTime](/abs/path/org/joda/time/MutableDateTime.java:722)
  - [MutableDateTime](/abs/path/org/joda/time/MutableDateTime.java:763)
- In `ZonedChronology`, `years`, `months`, `weeks`, and `days` are all wrapped as `ZonedDurationField`s during assembly:
  - [ZonedChronology](/abs/path/org/joda/time/chrono/ZonedChronology.java:154)
- The problematic method is:
  - [ZonedChronology](/abs/path/org/joda/time/chrono/ZonedChronology.java:314)

Why it fails:
- For date-based fields (`iTimeField == false`), `ZonedDurationField.add` does:
  1. take the current offset from the instant,
  2. convert the instant to local time,
  3. apply the field add,
  4. resolve local time back to UTC using `getOffsetFromLocal`.
- When `value == 0`, step 3 is a no-op, but step 4 still re-resolves the ambiguous local time during the DST overlap.
- In the failing case, the object is already on the winter-side occurrence of `2011-10-30T02:30` in `Europe/Berlin` (`+01:00`). Re-resolving that same local time can select the earlier summer offset (`+02:00`), so a no-op add changes the instant.

The root cause is that `ZonedDurationField.add(long, int)` does not preserve identity for `value == 0` on overlap-sensitive date fields. It should return the original `instant` for zero adds instead of recalculating the offset through ambiguous local time resolution.

m55.content:
The bug is in `org.joda.time.chrono.ZonedChronology.ZonedDurationField.add(long, int)`.

Static evidence:
- `MutableDateTime.addYears/addMonths/addWeeks/addDays/add(DurationFieldType, int)` all delegate directly to chronology duration fields:
  - [MutableDateTime](/abs/path/org/joda/time/MutableDateTime.java:635)
  - [MutableDateTime](/abs/path/org/joda/time/MutableDateTime.java:659)
  - [MutableDateTime](/abs/path/org/joda/time/MutableDateTime.java:701)
  - [MutableDateTime](/abs/path/org/joda/time/MutableDateTime.java:722)
  - [MutableDateTime](/abs/path/org/joda/time/MutableDateTime.java:763)
- In `ZonedChronology`, `years`, `months`, `weeks`, and `days` are all wrapped as `ZonedDurationField`s during assembly:
  - [ZonedChronology](/abs/path/org/joda/time/chrono/ZonedChronology.java:154)
- The problematic method is:
  - [ZonedChronology](/abs/path/org/joda/time/chrono/ZonedChronology.java:314)

Why it fails:
- For date-based fields (`iTimeField == false`), `ZonedDurationField.add` does:
  1. take the current offset from the instant,
  2. convert the instant to local time,
  3. apply the field add,
  4. resolve local time back to UTC using `getOffsetFromLocal`.
- When `value == 0`, step 3 is a no-op, but step 4 still re-resolves the ambiguous local time during the DST overlap.
- In the failing case, the object is already on the winter-side occurrence of `2011-10-30T02:30` in `Europe/Berlin` (`+01:00`). Re-resolving that same local time can select the earlier summer offset (`+02:00`), so a no-op add changes the instant.

The root cause is that `ZonedDurationField.add(long, int)` does not preserve identity for `value == 0` on overlap-sensitive date fields. It should return the original `instant` for zero adds instead of recalculating the offset through ambiguous local time resolution.
